newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China state-run TV "too busy" to cover HK protests.
newsitem.headline: China state-run TV "too busy" to cover HK protests.

text.p: Chinese viewers tuning into China Central Television (CCTV) reports on Hong Kong's handover on Monday won't catch a glimpse of any protests as the state-run network has more important things to cover, a top editor says.

"Compared to all the big things happening during the handover, they (the protesters) do not deserve a glance," chief editor Zhou Jing, who leads CCTV's 289-strong handover crew, told the Hong Kong Standard newspaper.
"We don't have time to deal with them. We have something more important to do."

Pro-democracy activists say they will protest outside the Convention Centre, where 4,000 VIPs will look on as Britain's Prince Charles hands back Hong Kong to Chinese President Jiang Zemin at midnight (1600 GMT).
They also plan a vigil at the Legislative Council building in the hours straddling the handover.

On Sunday, a small group of activists erected banners outside the Convention Centre, calling on China to free dissidents and condemning the Beijing-backed provisional legislature that will replace Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council.
CCTV's coverage would be "objective" despite the omission of the protesters, Zhou said.

The network's Chinese-language channels began 72 hours of live handover coverage at 6 a.m. on Monday (2200 GMT on Sunday). Its English-language channels began 41 hours of similar programming 55 miniutes later.
